headline: Public omics data nominate hub genes and compounds across inflammatory and renal disease
label: Computational Hub Gene Prioritization
summary: Pipelines pairing single-cell data, machine learning and docking are now generating candidate targets from public datasets across multiple disease areas.
synthesis: The dominant thread is computational prioritization of candidate genes and compounds from public omics data, usually followed by a limited experimental or in silico check. Several items pair transcriptomic data with differential expression, WGCNA or machine learning feature selection, then molecular docking or dynamics: GLS and LPIN2 in renal fibroblasts for kidney stones, five hub genes with two docked lead compounds in ligamentum flavum hypertrophy, CD36-associated macrophages in diabetic nephropathy, and a PFKFB3-centered network with salidroside binding in coronary heart disease. Others add Mendelian randomization, as with BLMH in psoriasis and IGFBP4, IL1B and LAPTM5 in periodontitis, or shared-gene analysis of psoriasis and ischemic stroke nominating TLR2 and TNFSF10. The new content lies mainly in specific gene, compound and disease pairings rather than analytical methods. The myeloma exosomal circ_0002724 and periodontitis CD8 effector T cell studies depend less on this pipeline, tracing defined regulatory axes instead.
